subject.title: Android node notification forwarding causes cross-session replies (WhatsApp duplicate sends to wrong group)

question: Should OpenClaw primarily fix this by enforcing outbound session/channel binding for node notification sessions, by suppressing native-channel packages in Android/Gateway notification forwarding, or by combining both?
rationale: The source path crosses Android notification policy, Gateway node events, and outbound message-tool authority; automation should not choose that security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Harden Outbound Binding First
options.body: Reject or constrain cross-channel message sends from node notification sessions unless an explicit operator-approved route binding exists, then use Android/Gateway filtering as defense in depth.

options.title: Suppress Native Packages First
options.body: Block known native-channel app packages before `notifications.changed` reaches node sessions, accepting package-list and plugin-discovery maintenance risk.

options.title: Add Operator Filter Only
options.body: Expose Android or Gateway package exclusion configuration and leave route binding unchanged, which helps advanced operators but does not close the default authority boundary by itself.

recommendation.title: Harden Outbound Binding First
recommendation.body: Reject or constrain cross-channel message sends from node notification sessions unless an explicit operator-approved route binding exists, then use Android/Gateway filtering as defense in depth.

likelyOwner.reason: The earliest current feature history for Android notification events and Gateway node-event routing points to this owner path, with Android policy and outbound-policy owners as adjacent reviewers.
